chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the wicked (immoral) woman, can I marry her? He said: No.

key_terms.الْخَبِيثَةِ: The wicked/immoral woman (feminine form of khabith)

ai.seo_question: Can I marry an immoral woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on marrying a 'khabithah,' a term in Shia jurisprudence often referring to a woman of known moral laxity or promiscuity. The Imam’s concise 'No' establishes a strong discouragement (or prohibition, depending on the juristic interpretation of 'khabithah' versus 'zaniyah') based on the principle of selecting a spouse of good character (khusn al-khilqah). This highlights the Shia emphasis on moral integrity (adab) as a primary criterion in marriage, extending beyond mere lineage.
